title: Kaempferol ameliorates septic coronary microvascular injury through PHB2-PKM2 mediated mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum homeostasis.
authors: Pu, Xiangyi; Zhang, Xinai; Yan, Zhaoqi; Guan, Xuanke; Liu, Jinfeng; Wang, Yanli; Wu, Qiaomin; Zhou, Siyuan; Liu, Zhiming; Liu, Ruxiu; Chang, Xing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究山奈酚通过PHB2-PKM2通路改善脓毒症冠脉微血管损伤，核心是线粒体/内质网稳态与炎症，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，仅分子对接为辅助验证，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial dysfunction and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress are pivotal contributors to coronary microvascular injury. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has shown remarkable advantages in treating coronary microvascular injury. Nevertheless, the exact mechanisms by which KA exerts its effects, especially through the Prohibitin 2 (PHB2) and pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) pathway for treating coronary microvascular injury in sepsis, are still not well understood. This study aims to investigate the mechanism by which KA modulates mitochondrial and ER homeostasis through the PHB2/PKM2 pathway, thereby ameliorating septic coronary microvascular injury. METHOD: PHB2-specific knockout (PHB2(cko)) and transgenic (PHB2(tg)) mouse models, along with coronary microvascular endothelial cell models with PHB2 knockdown (siRNA-PHB2), PHB2 overexpression (ad-PHB2), PKM2 knockdown (siRNA-PKM2), and PKM2 overexpression (ad-PKM2), were utilized to explore the roles of Kaempferol in septic coronary microvascular injury. RESULTS: KA treatment enhanced mitochondrial stability, modulated the mitochondrial quality control (MQC) system, inhibited calcium overload, and attenuated cardiac inflammation and myocardial microvascular dysfunction through the PHB2/PKM2 pathway. Molecular docking confirmed the direct interaction between PHB2 and PKM2 and the target of KA action. CONCLUSION: KA plays a protective role against septic coronary microvascular injury by regulating MQC, inhibiting ER stress injury, and balancing mitochondria and ER homeostasis through the PHB2/PKM2 signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: 背景：线粒体功能障碍和内质网（ER）应激是冠状动脉微血管损伤的关键诱因。传统中药（TCM）在治疗冠状动脉微血管损伤方面显示出显著优势。然而，KA发挥其作用的确切机制，特别是通过Prohibitin 2（PHB2）和丙酮酸激酶M2（PKM2）通路治疗脓毒症中冠状动脉微血管损伤的机制，仍尚未完全阐明。本研究旨在探讨KA通过PHB2/PKM2通路调节线粒体和内质网稳态，从而改善脓毒性冠状动脉微血管损伤的机制。方法：利用PHB2特异性敲除（PHB2(cko)）和转基因（PHB2(tg)）小鼠模型，以及PHB2敲低（siRNA-PHB2）、PHB2过表达（ad-PHB2）、PKM2敲低（siRNA-PKM2）和PKM2过表达（ad-PKM2）的冠状动脉微血管内皮细胞模型，探讨山奈酚在脓毒性冠状动脉微血管损伤中的作用。结果：KA处理通过PHB2/PKM2通路增强了线粒体稳定性，调节了线粒体质量控制（MQC）系统，抑制了钙超载，并减轻了心脏炎症和心肌微血管功能障碍。分子对接证实了PHB2与PKM2之间的直接相互作用以及KA作用的靶点。结论：KA通过调节MQC、抑制ER应激损伤，并通过PHB2/PKM2信号通路平衡线粒体和内质网稳态，对脓毒性冠状动脉微血管损伤发挥保护作用。
